label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**Northvale froze your money. Here's what happened, and what you can do now.**

*By Inês, Pinha · Tuesday 10 November 2026*

I'm writing this instead of Rui because he has been on calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal since early this morning, and someone needed to tell you properly what is going on. I write most of the words you see in the app, so it's me.

I'll say the important part first, because some of you will stop reading after this paragraph.

**Your money is not lost. Right now you can't take it out. That is wrong, and we are fighting to fix it.**

If you need money urgently for rent, medical costs, losing your job, or anything that can't wait, write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**. More on that below.

### What happened

Pinha doesn't hold your money itself. Since we started, the money you save through round-ups has been held by our payments partner, Northvale Payments, an e-money institution in Vilnius. It sits in what's called a safeguarded account. That means it's kept separate from Northvale's own money, and Northvale isn't allowed to use it for anything. It's yours.

On **Wednesday 4 November**, Northvale emailed us to say they were ending our contract, with 30 days' notice. They didn't give a real reason, only the words "risk appetite review". We weren't happy, but 30 days is enough time to move everyone to a new partner without you noticing much. We started working on it that same day.

On **Friday 6 November at 09:00**, without any warning, Northvale blocked every outgoing transfer from Pinha accounts. Deposits and round-ups stopped too. This was two days after they promised us 30 days. Their own notice said one thing and they did another.

Since that Friday, our account manager at Northvale has stopped answering. Their phone goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian.

I'll be honest with you about how I see it. This isn't "risk". When a company gives a 30-day notice and then breaks it two days later, and then stops picking up the phone, that's cowardice. Real people's money is on the other side of that decision.

### Where your money is right now

Your money is still in the safeguarded account at Northvale. They can't spend it, lend it, or mix it with their own funds. That protection exists exactly for moments like this.

What safeguarding does *not* do is let us move it ourselves. Until Northvale releases it, we can't send it to you or anywhere else. I know "it's safe but you can't touch it" is a terrible thing to hear when you need it. I'm not going to pretend it's good news. It's only the less bad news.

### What we're doing

**A new partner is already signed.** We've signed with Ostra Bank in Lisbon. The plan is to move every Pinha balance from Northvale to Ostra, and after that you'll be able to withdraw normally again.

For that to happen we need two things:
1. Northvale has to send us the balances file (the official record of how much belongs to each of you).
2. Banco de Portugal has to approve the migration.

**How long?** Our current estimate is 10 to 15 working days. I want to be very clear that this is an estimate and **not a promise**. Most of it depends on Northvale, who have already broken one promise to us this week. I won't give you a date I can't keep. I'd rather tell you the truth and update you often.

**We filed formal complaints** with Banco de Portugal and with the Bank of Lithuania (Lietuvos bankas), Northvale's regulator, on Saturday 7 November. Rui and our lawyers are pushing on both every day.

**We're trying to get individual releases for urgent cases.** We're asking Northvale and the regulators to let money out for people in serious situations before the full migration. I can't promise this will work, but we're trying for every single urgent case.

**No fees for November and December.** We've cancelled the monthly fee for everyone for both months. You don't need to do anything. I know this is small next to what you're dealing with. It's just the one thing we can fully control right now.

### If you need your money urgently

Write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**.

Please tell us:
- what you need the money for (rent, medical, job loss, a deadline you can't move)
- how much you need
- the date you need it by

We read these first, before anything else, and we use them to push for individual releases.

One of you wrote to us this weekend, all in capitals, and I understood why. She has been saving for three years for a car deposit, and the dealer gave her until this Friday. I read her email on the metro and nearly cried. We're doing everything we can for her and for everyone in a situation like hers. I won't tell you we'll definitely make it in time, because I don't know that yet.

### About our support inbox

Since Friday we've received around 1,900 emails. We're a team of three answering them, and right now replies take about 2 days. I'm sorry it's that slow. Every email is being read by a real person, and none of them are being ignored.

If you've already written to us, you don't need to write again. A second email won't move you up the queue, and it makes the queue longer for everyone. If your situation has become urgent since you wrote, use the URGENTE address.

### Our part in this

Northvale broke their word. But I'm not going to write a whole post blaming them and pretend we did nothing wrong.

We had one payments partner and no backup. If that one partner failed, everything would stop, and it did. That was naive, and it was our mistake. A company that holds other people's savings should have had a second option ready long before a week like this one. We didn't, and you're the ones paying for it.

I designed the screen in the app that says *"your money is always yours, take it out anytime."* I look at it now and I feel sick. The first part is still true. The money is yours. The second part isn't true right now, and I wrote it. I'm sorry.

When this is over, having only one partner will never happen again. We'll explain exactly how we're changing that once you have your money back. Right now your money matters more than our plans.

### You're allowed to be angry

You're allowed to be angry with Northvale, and with us. I'm not going to ask you to be patient or to calm down. You trusted us with your savings, and right now you can't reach them. Anger is the normal reaction. We're angry too, and we're putting that into getting your money out.

### When you'll hear from us

We'll post an update here on the blog **every Monday and Thursday** until this is solved. The next one is this **Thursday, 12 November**. If something important happens in between, like Northvale sending the file, a release for urgent cases, or a decision from Banco de Portugal, we'll post it straight away and not wait for the next update day.

Every update will tell you what changed, what didn't, and what we still don't know.

To sum up:
- **Your money is safeguarded and not lost**, but you can't withdraw it yet.
- **Urgent?** Email **urgent@pinha.example**, subject **URGENTE**, with what you need, how much, and by when.
- **Already emailed support?** No need to write again. Replies take about 2 days right now.
- **No fees** for November and December.
- **Next update:** Thursday 12 November, here on the blog.

Inês
Pinha

---

A few things to check before it goes up:

- **The date.** Today is Wednesday 11 November, and the post says Tuesday 10. If it's going out today, change it to 11 November. The "next update Thursday 12 November" line still works either way.
- **The woman from Porto.** I took out the city on purpose. A three-year car deposit with a deadline this Friday, plus "Porto", could be enough for people who know her to recognise her. Even without the city, it's worth asking her if she's OK with being mentioned. If you can't reach her, you can cut that paragraph and the post still works.
- **"Cowardice."** I kept it because it's your honest opinion and it's clearly written as opinion. But Rui is with lawyers today about this exact company, so let them see the Northvale paragraphs for two minutes before you publish. A sentence like that could be used against you in the dispute.
- **"Bank of Lithuania (Lietuvos bankas)."** Your notes say "Lithuanian central bank", so I used the official name. Check it matches what you actually filed with.
